profile.campus: Papillion, Sarpy County, Nebraska (Google's original Nebraska data center campus, broke ground late 2019 on 275 acres, 14706 Schram Road)
profile.address: Schram Road, Papillion, Richland VIII Precinct, Sarpy County, Nebraska, 68046
profile.reading:
This building sits on Schram Road in Papillion, matching Google's own address for its original Nebraska data center campus, 14706 Schram Road, which broke ground on 275 acres in late 2019 at a reported cost of roughly $600 million, Google's first Nebraska facility. Google has continued to expand the Papillion site in the years since, and a company spokesperson has described staff progression from Papillion into leadership roles at Google's newer Lincoln, Nebraska campus, illustrating how the original site anchored Google's broader Nebraska workforce. Since 2019, Google has created more than 120 jobs across computer technician, engineer, maintenance, and food service roles at its Nebraska sites, which the company has said it declines to break out by individual location. Google reports investing about $4.4 billion in Nebraska cumulatively over the five years through 2024, including $930 million in 2024 alone, spread across the Papillion, northwest Omaha, and Lincoln campuses. Google's own Nebraska data center location page does not identify which specific building on the Papillion campus this OSM-mapped structure corresponds to, nor its individual square footage or MW capacity, so this registry records the $4.4 billion statewide figure as regional context rather than a fact specific to this building, and flags a Sarpy County Assessor parcel lookup as the next real research step.

Omaha Public Power District, which serves the Douglas and Sarpy county campuses, has cited large-load data center demand from Google and other operators as a leading factor in its own long-range generation and transmission planning, and Nebraska's status as one of the few states where electricity is delivered entirely by public power districts rather than investor-owned utilities has repeatedly come up in coverage of why Google, Facebook, and other hyperscalers chose the Omaha-Lincoln corridor for a dense cluster of campuses.

reading.body:
Google operates a data center campus in Sarpy County as part of its broader Omaha-area presence spanning Douglas County and Sarpy County, Nebraska. The company does not publish individual facility power capacity, square footage, or street addresses; it discloses only aggregate state-level investment figures. A Papillion data center within this campus area was reported at approximately $600 million in local reporting, though this figure is not an official Google specification.

No megawatt capacity is published for this facility, making it impossible to estimate its rack or accelerator count or to compare its scale to other data center campuses. Nebraska has 21 mapped data center facilities across the state, but none of them, including this Google campus, publish power consumption figures on their specification pages. This campus ranks first among published capacity in Nebraska only because no other facility in the state has disclosed a megawatt figure.

The campus sits within a Sarpy County data center corridor that also hosts Yahoo, Travelers, and other operators. Without published power specifications, this campus cannot be ranked against other AI-relevant data center investments or assessed for its significance to national compute infrastructure and grid demand.
